terminal_record.title: Internal Draft — Unverified Tariff and Price Allegations
terminal_record.description_short: The supplied entry alleges a 6% price rise after tariffs and attempted data suppression; its CPI contradiction and claimed household effects remain unverified.
terminal_record.description_medium: The supplied entry alleges that consumer prices rose 6% in a few months by late August 2025 after new tariffs, that this erased savings for middle- and working-class households, and that the administration tried to suppress the related data. A prior review in the packet disputes the 6% figure, citing August CPI readings of 0.4% month over month and 2.9% year over year; the packet provides no source URL or excerpt for those numbers. The allegations and copied date remain unverified.
terminal_record.description_long: The frozen entry places the allegation on August 26, 2025, and says consumer prices had risen 6% in a few months after new tariffs. It also alleges that this increase wiped out the savings of middle- and working-class households and that the administration tried to suppress the related economic data. These are claims in the supplied record; this internal draft does not establish that prices rose by 6%, that tariffs caused a specific increase, that households lost savings, or that an official tried to suppress a release. A prior review in the packet disputes the 6% figure, citing August 2025 CPI readings of 0.4% month over month and 2.9% year over year, but provides no source URL or excerpt. The packet gives no measurement series or time window for the 6% claim, no household-level evidence, and no document identifying an alleged suppression attempt. It therefore leaves both the numerical contradiction and the underlying allegations unresolved. The date is copied from the frozen entry and is not independently verified. Publication eligibility remains false, and impact scoring is deferred because the event and its effects are not established.
